full_judgment: 3. The appellant in Criminal Appeal Nos.1-3 were convicted under Section 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 and were sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for 7 years along with other co-accused by the judgment and order dated 7-6-1993. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the plot No.49 and 49A situated at Karwan Bazar Commercial Area each plot measuring 21 kathas were put to auction by the DIT/RAJUK on 5-6-1985. Accused Abdus Sukur Prodhan offered the highest bid of Taka 1,93,550 per katha for plot No.49 and one Golam Kibria offered Taka 1,92,000 per katha for the other plot. The DIT, as then it was, considered the offer inadequate and decided to construct a building of its own on the said two plots. Subsequently when the DIT/RAJUK took steps to re-auction the two plots three suits were filed by some of the previous bidders challenging the re-auction and obtained an order of injunction. While the suits were pending accused Abdus Sukur Prodhan and 12 others filed a petition on 26-8-1989 directly to the former President HM Ershad praying for allotment of the plots on the ground that they were affected persons and they had offered the highest bid in the auction held earlier. The former President within two days passed an order of 29-8-1989 on the body of the petition to the effect. ‘দরখাস্তকারীর বিগত সর্ব্বোচ্চ নিলাম ডাকে ও ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হিসাবে দরখাস্তকারীদের মধ্যে প্লট বরাদ্দ করা হোক। The order of the former President HM Ershad was forwarded to Chairman, RAJUK who on 12-9-1989 alloted the aforesaid lands in groups at the rate of Taka 1,93,550 per katha in favour of the accused Abdus Sukur Prodhan, Md Sekander Hussain, Abdul Wadud Khan, Abraham Purification, Md Shafiqul Islam, Md Jahangir Alam, Md Khalilur Rahman, Mrs Lovely Begum, Md Nawab Miah, Md Abu Hanif Shahinoor Islam, Mosammat Aftara Begum and one Sadeque Hossain dividing the plot into four plots i.e. Nos.49, 49A, 49B and 49C. Plot No. 49 with an area of 12 kathas was allotted to accused Shahinoor Islam, Aftara Begum and one Sadeque Hussain at a total price of Taka 23,33,600. The money was deposited on 18-9-1989, possession of the land was delivered on 19-9-1989 in favour of the lessees and lease deed was registered on 21-10-1989. On the very next day i.e. 22-10-1989 the lessee sought permission of the RAJUK to transfer plot No.49 in favour of Janata Publishers Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as JPL) for a total consideration of Taka 33,00,000. On 25-10-1989 the RAJUK accorded permission for transfer. The deed was registered on 2-11-1989 in favour of the JPL. It is alleged that Md Sadeque Hussain was residing abroad at the relevant time and accused Akjadul Haq forged the signature of Sadeque Hossain on the lease deed and did everything in the name of the said absentee Sadeque Hussain by false personification including forging his signature in the deed of sale in favour of Janata Publishers Ltd. It is further alleged that although in the transfer deed the total price was shown as Taka 33,00,000 the transferors Shahinoor Islam, Aftara Begum and Amjadul Haque did not receive any money from the JPL and they only received Taka 1,63,000 from Abdus Sukur Prodhan. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka by his Memo dated 8-10-1989 informed the RAJUK that none of the above mentioned allottees were original affected persons. It is further alleged that in order to get allotment the allottee must be an original affected person. It is clear from the letter of the ADC (Revenue) Dhaka dated 8-10-1989 that none of the applicants was original affected person. The former President without verifying the truth of the statements and without taking steps for such verification passed order for giving allotments to these persons directly which was illegal. It was further alleged that no transfer could be made without construction on the land, but in this case impediment was overcome by RAJUK by amending paragraph 20 of the standard lease deed on 22-10-1989. It was alleged that these allotments were made with the ulterior motive to give the land to Janata Publishers Ltd of which accused Rawshan Ara Begum was the Chairperson and accused Abdus Sattar former Minister and Chief Whip was a Director. It was alleged that the former President HM Ershad and M. M Rahmatullah in collusion with each other dishonestly and fraudulently with malafide intention helped the 13 accused applicants to get illegally the lease of the land in their favour and then helped JPL and its Directors to get 12 kathas of land of plot No. 49 at a negligible sum causing loss to RAJUK to the tune of Taka 5,48,70,900 to obtain pecuniary advantage for themselves or for others. All other accused acted illegally in collusion with each other to obtain a pecuniary advantage. By the allotment of the aforesaid land to those claimed to be affected persons, the former President HM Ershad and M. M Rahmatullah former Chairman of DIT have caused a loss of Taka 5,48,70,900 to DIT (RAJUK) by corrupt or illegal means or by otherwise abusing their position as public servants had obtained for themselves or the appellants and others pecuniary advantage of the same amount and the appellants have committed the offence of abetment as they have obtained pecuniary advantage and thereby they have committed an offence punishable under section 109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.
